title: 'Will' in if- and time clauses
what: putting 'will' or 'would' in the if-clause or time clause ('If it will rain, we stay inside', 'When I will arrive, I call you', 'If I would know')
summary: This error persists because context often clarifies meaning, making it less noticeable. However, it subtly detracts from fluency and precision, signaling a non-native command of advanced English grammar.
listenFor: Pay close attention to whether you use 'will' or 'would' immediately following conjunctions like 'if', 'when', 'as soon as', or 'until'.

contrasts.wrong: If it will rain tomorrow, we should reschedule the outdoor event.
contrasts.right: If it rains tomorrow, we should reschedule the outdoor event.
contrasts.note: Use simple present in the if-clause for future conditions.

contrasts.wrong: When I will finish this report, I will send it to the team.
contrasts.right: When I finish this report, I will send it to the team.
contrasts.note: Use simple present in time clauses referring to the future.

contrasts.wrong: As soon as she will arrive, we can begin the presentation.
contrasts.right: As soon as she arrives, we can begin the presentation.
contrasts.note: Simple present for future actions in time clauses.

contrasts.wrong: If I would know the answer, I would certainly tell you.
contrasts.right: If I knew the answer, I would certainly tell you.
contrasts.note: Use simple past in the if-clause for hypothetical present conditions.

contrasts.wrong: Until the new policy will be implemented, we must follow the old guidelines.
contrasts.right: Until the new policy is implemented, we must follow the old guidelines.
contrasts.note: Simple present for future events in time clauses.

contrasts.wrong: I will inform you if there will be any changes to the schedule.
contrasts.right: I will inform you if there are any changes to the schedule.
contrasts.note: Simple present for future conditions in if-clauses.

When the project concludes, we will evaluate its overall impact.

probes.sentence: If he will accept the offer, we can start negotiations immediately.
answers: If he accepts the offer, we can start negotiations immediately.

probes.sentence: I will call you back as soon as I will finish this urgent task.
answers: I will call you back as soon as I finish this urgent task.

probes.sentence: If I would have more time, I would dedicate it to learning a new skill.
answers: If I had more time, I would dedicate it to learning a new skill.

probes.sentence: They will not leave until the final decision will be made.
answers: They will not leave until the final decision is made.

answers: We will proceed with the plan if the board gives its approval.

answers: When the new system is fully operational, efficiency will greatly improve.
